title: Product law implies conditioning on Bob's special bit leaves Alice's law unchanged
statement: Fix a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$ and an achievable value $z$ of the record $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$, and write $\mu_z$ for the hard distribution conditioned on the fiber $Z=z$. Let $X_T$ and $Y_T$ denote Alice's and Bob's bits at the special coordinate $T$, and suppose that under $\mu_z$ the pair $(X_T,Y_T)$ has product law, i.e. the law of $(X_T,Y_T)$ equals the product of the law of $X_T$ and the law of $Y_T$. Then for every $b_Y\in\{\text{false},\text{true}\}$ such that the event $\{Y_T=b_Y\}$ has positive $\mu_z$-mass, the law of $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ coincides with the law of $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ conditioned further on $\{Y_T=b_Y\}$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic disjointness protocol on inputs of length n
z is an achievable value of the Z variable
the fiber (conditional) measure at Z = z
the conditional law of the special pair (X_T, Y_T) equals the product of the conditional laws of X_T and Y_T
the event Y_T = b_Y has positive mass under the fiber measure
replaced: On a product-law $Z$ fiber, conditioning on one Bob special-bit value does not change Alice's special-bit law.
